Well, let's break up your request into two parts. First, it is already possible now to have a pretty deep relationship with someone over the internet that you have never met (over the internet in chat rooms this has been going on for years). So that part is realistic; even if what you can do with it is limited (you won't have the closeness of human contact or be able to do much besides talk over the internet, so a lot of what makes a relationship will still be off limits).

Second, can you completely replace the other human at the other end with a computer program to talk to you? I think so, but again, this will have limits. A computer can certainly be programmed to respond to you, and can use your prior responses to create future responses much like what they do with advanced chess AI programs. It can also be programmed to start conversations (say scanning the web and telling you about a news story it read). The real problem is the same problem chess AI programs have, it can scan a database of data but it has problems "creating" and being spontaneous. So yeah, you would have interaction, but at least at present it would seem pretty robotic and uninteresting. To get to the level where it has human emotion the computer would have to produce feedback with itself and be able to create a response for you based on that feedback. I am not saying it can't be done, but the technology for that isn't here yet.
